habitImpact.title: What science tells us
habitImpact.subtitle: What your logs support, what research measured, and what is still unknown about your individual case.

sleepShort.title: Sleep below 7 hours
sleepShort.message: You logged {{hours}} hours: {{deficit}} hours below the usual 7-hour minimum for adults and {{differenceFromReference}} hours below an 8-hour reference. A meta-analysis of 44 studies quantified effects after one night with a 2–6 hour sleep opportunity: sleepiness (SMD 0.986), reaction time (SMD 0.512), and attentional lapses (SMD 0.489). These are standardised group effects, not percentages or an individual prediction.

sleepRange.title: Recorded sleep duration
sleepRange.message: You logged {{hours}} hours, within the usual 7–9 hour reference for adults. Individual needs vary; this entry alone does not measure sleep quality or nervous-system function.

sleepLong.title: Sleep above 9 hours
sleepLong.message: You logged {{hours}} hours. Sleeping more than 9 hours is not automatically a problem; it can be appropriate during recovery from sleep loss or in other circumstances. Duration alone cannot establish the cause.

exercise.title: Physical activity — last 7 days
exercise.message: Today you logged {{todayMinutes}} minutes across {{sessions}} session(s). In the last 7 days: {{moderate}} min of moderate activity (minimum reference: {{moderateTarget}} min/week), {{vigorous}} min of vigorous activity (minimum reference: {{vigorousTarget}} min/week), {{strengthDays}} muscle-strengthening days (reference: {{strengthTarget}} days), and {{unclassified}} min of light or unspecified intensity, which are not added to those targets.

caffeine.title: Estimated caffeine
caffeine.message: Based on the types and quantities logged, the estimate is {{mg}} mg of caffeine, about {{percentage}}% of EFSA’s 400 mg/day reference for most healthy adults. Older entries without serving details use typical category values. This is an estimate, not a measurement of the product consumed.

caffeineLate.title: Caffeine logged late in the day
caffeineLate.message: Caffeine was logged at a late time. EFSA notes that a single 100 mg dose may affect sleep in some people, especially close to bedtime. Confia may not know your bedtime or exact dose, so the effect cannot be calculated for this entry.

produce.title: Fruit and vegetables — recommendation comparison
produce.message: You logged {{value}} {{unit}}. WHO’s reference is at least {{reference}} {{unit}} per day for people older than 10. This comparison uses only quantities explicitly recorded in grams or portions; individual items are not converted into assumed weights.

produceUnquantified.title: Fruit and vegetables without a comparable quantity
produceUnquantified.message: You logged fruit or vegetables, but the amount is recorded as items rather than grams or portions. I will not estimate the weight or claim you met or missed WHO’s recommendation.

water.title: Water logged
water.message: You logged approximately {{ml}} ml of water. Portugal’s DGS gives 1,500 ml/day as general practical guidance, but needs vary and this log may not include all fluids. This value does not diagnose dehydration.

fastFood.title: Fast food logged
fastFood.message: WHO does not set a specific daily amount for fast food. It recommends a varied diet with fruit, vegetables, pulses and whole grains, while limiting foods high in salt, free sugars and unhealthy fats. Prefer simple, minimally processed meals.

sweets.title: Sweets logged
sweets.message: WHO recommends keeping free sugars below 10% of daily energy and ideally below 5%. For a 2,000 kcal diet, that is about 50 g and 25 g per day, respectively. This reference includes free sugars from all foods and drinks, not sweets alone.

salt.title: Salty foods logged
salt.message: For adults, WHO recommends less than 5 g of salt per day (less than 2,000 mg sodium). Check food labels and limit very salty foods, preferring fresh or minimally processed options.

alcohol.title: Alcohol logged
alcohol.message: WHO states that no level of alcohol consumption is risk-free. From a health perspective, less alcohol means lower risk; daily drinking is not recommended.

tobacco.title: Tobacco logged
tobacco.message: WHO states that all forms of tobacco use are harmful and that there is no safe level of exposure. The health recommendation is to avoid tobacco and exposure to tobacco smoke.

cereals.title: Cereals logged
cereals.message: WHO recommends choosing whole grains rather than refined grains as part of a varied diet. Options include oats, wholegrain bread and brown rice; pay attention to fibre and added sugars.

protein.title: Protein sources logged
protein.message: WHO recommends a varied diet. Rotate protein sources, including pulses (beans, chickpeas and lentils), nuts, fish and other options suited to your needs.

fats.title: Fats logged
fats.message: WHO generally recommends total fat at no more than 30% of daily energy, saturated fat below 10%, and trans fat below 1%. Prefer unsaturated fats, such as olive oil, nuts and seeds, over trans fats and excess saturated fats.

soda.title: Soft drinks logged
soda.message: WHO recommends keeping free sugars below 10% of daily energy and ideally below 5%. Sugar-sweetened drinks contribute to this total; prefer water and unsweetened drinks.

habitLog.title: Your habit entry
habitLog.message: Habit: “{{habitName}}”. Your stated goal: “{{goal}}”. This entry records whether you marked the goal as met, but does not automatically measure dose, duration, or physiological effect. Quantified analysis requires an observable measure.

caffeineUnknown.title: Caffeine cannot be quantified from this entry
caffeineUnknown.message: The recorded type or serving does not support a reliable caffeine estimate. Amounts vary substantially across products and sizes, so I will not present a typical dose as if it were exact.

nutrientDetailLimit.title: Nutritional composition not recorded
nutrientDetailLimit.message: The entry stores a category and quantity, but not the nutrition-label values. Exact calories or grams of sugar, salt, or saturated fat therefore cannot be calculated from this entry.

waterUnknown.title: Water logged without a comparable volume
waterUnknown.message: This older entry contains a water count but no volume in ml or serving size. I will not convert the count into litres without knowing the cup or bottle size.

sleepDetails.title: Recorded sleep quality and awakenings
sleepDetails.message: Along with duration, you rated sleep quality {{quality}}/5 and recorded {{awakenings}} awakenings. These self-reports help compare patterns, but do not measure sleep stages or diagnose a disorder.
sleepDetails.qualityOnly: You rated sleep quality {{quality}}/5. This is a subjective rating; it does not measure sleep stages or diagnose a disorder.

personal.title: What appears in your history
personal.intro: Exploratory comparison of your own emotional ratings on days with different levels of measured habits. Missing consumption or activity is never assumed.
personal.exercise: 30+ minutes of exercise on logged days
personal.pattern: In your logs, average emotional-state rating was {{direction}} on days with {{condition}} ({{exposedMean}}/10; {{exposedDays}} days) than on comparison days ({{comparisonMean}}/10; {{comparisonDays}} days). Observed difference: {{difference}} points.
personal.caution: This is an association in your history, not proof that the habit caused the change. The 200 mg caffeine and 30-minute exercise cut-offs are analytical groupings, not clinical limits or recommendations. Exercise comparisons include only days with logged sessions; days without logs are never treated as no activity. Other factors and incomplete logs may affect the results.
personal.insufficient: There is not enough data for an exploratory personal comparison yet. At least 10 measured days in each group and an emotional rating on those same days are required. Missing logs are never treated as zero. Emotional-rating days available in the last 30 days: {{count}}.
personal.water: At least 1,500 ml of logged water
personal.produce: At least 400 g or 5 portions of fruit and vegetables

sleepRestriction.title: Impact of one night of sleep restriction on sleepiness and cognitive function: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sleepRestriction.evidenceType: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 44 studies
sleepRestriction.population: Adults; sleep opportunity restricted to 2–6 hours for one night
sleepRestriction.statistic: One night of restricted sleep increased subjective sleepiness (standardised mean difference 0.986) and impaired sustained attention: reaction time SMD 0.512 and attentional lapses SMD 0.489.
sleepRestriction.certainty: Evidence of short-term effects on sleepiness and sustained attention; effects varied by cognitive outcome.
sleepRestriction.limitations: Standardised mean differences are not percentages and do not predict an individual’s reaction time or emotional state.

adultSleep.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult: A Joint Consensus Statement
adultSleep.organization: American Academy of Sleep Medicine / Sleep Research Society
adultSleep.statistic: Adults should sleep 7 or more hours per night regularly to promote optimal health.
adultSleep.certainty: Consensus recommendation supported by a review of health outcomes.
adultSleep.limitations: Individual sleep needs and occasional recovery needs vary; a single short night is not a diagnosis.

caffeine.title: Caffeine
caffeine.evidenceType: Scientific risk assessment and public guidance
caffeine.population: Healthy adults; not applicable to every medical condition or pregnancy
caffeine.statistic: Up to 400 mg per day across the day does not raise safety concerns for most healthy adults; a single dose of 100 mg may affect sleep in some adults, particularly close to bedtime.
caffeine.certainty: Official population-level guidance; individual sensitivity varies.
caffeine.limitations: Confia’s caffeine amounts are estimates from typical serving values, not laboratory measurements or product-label data.

physicalActivity.title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour: at a glance
physicalActivity.evidenceType: Public health guideline based on evidence review
physicalActivity.statistic: WHO recommends 150–300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity per week, or 75–150 minutes of vigorous activity, and muscle-strengthening activity on at least 2 days per week.
physicalActivity.certainty: Public health recommendation; any activity is better than none.
physicalActivity.limitations: Minutes logged without intensity cannot be reliably counted as moderate or vigorous activity. Individual ability and medical context matter.

fruitVegetables.title: Healthy diet
fruitVegetables.statistic: WHO recommends at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables per day for people older than 10 years.
fruitVegetables.limitations: Counts of individual items cannot be converted accurately into grams without portion or weight information.

hydrationPortugal.title: Conheça os Alimentos — Dia Alimentar Completo, Equilibrado e Variado
hydrationPortugal.organization: National Programme for the Promotion of Healthy Eating (DGS), Portugal
hydrationPortugal.population: General public; needs vary by circumstances
hydrationPortugal.statistic: DGS public guidance suggests drinking at least 1.5 litres of water per day and increasing intake in heat or with exercise.
hydrationPortugal.certainty: Practical general guidance, not an individual hydration test.
hydrationPortugal.limitations: Logged water is not total fluid intake; needs vary with body size, diet, temperature, activity and health.

ultraProcessedFood.title: Ultra-processed food exposure and adverse health outcomes: umbrella review of epidemiological meta-analyses
ultraProcessedFood.evidenceType: Umbrella review of 45 pooled analyses, including 9,888,373 participants
ultraProcessedFood.population: Population studies; exposure to ultra-processed foods
ultraProcessedFood.statistic: Greater ultra-processed-food exposure was associated with prevalent anxiety outcomes (odds ratio 1.48, 95% CI 1.37–1.59); evidence quality for this outcome was rated low.
ultraProcessedFood.certainty: Association; evidence quality low for the anxiety outcome.
ultraProcessedFood.limitations: An odds ratio is not an individual percentage increase in anxiety. A generic fast-food log does not establish NOVA processing class or quantify exposure.

freeSugar.title: Healthy diet
freeSugar.statistic: WHO recommends limiting free sugars to less than 10% of daily energy intake, ideally 5% or less. For an adult consuming 2,000 kcal/day, 10% is approximately 50 g.
freeSugar.limitations: Confia currently records occasions or quantities of sweets, not the grams of free sugar or total daily energy needed to calculate this percentage.

salt.title: Healthy diet / Sodium reduction
salt.statistic: WHO recommends less than 2,000 mg sodium per day, equivalent to less than 5 g of salt. High sodium intake is associated with raised blood pressure and increased cardiovascular risk.
salt.limitations: The current Confia category records salty foods or occasions, not product sodium content or total daily salt intake.

tobacco.title: Tobacco and nicotine
tobacco.population: People who use tobacco and people exposed to second-hand smoke
tobacco.statistic: WHO reports that tobacco kills more than 7 million people each year and that all forms of tobacco use are harmful; there is no safe level of exposure.
tobacco.limitations: A generic category count does not identify the product, nicotine content, quantity or duration, so it cannot estimate individual exposure or risk.

gamingDisorder.title: Gaming disorder
gamingDisorder.evidenceType: International disease classification and expert review
gamingDisorder.population: People whose gaming pattern causes significant impairment in functioning
gamingDisorder.statistic: WHO defines gaming disorder by impaired control, gaming taking priority over other activities, and continuing despite negative consequences; the pattern must cause significant impairment and is normally evident for at least 12 months.
gamingDisorder.certainty: Clinical classification; not a threshold for ordinary gaming duration.
gamingDisorder.limitations: Gaming or a single gaming session does not imply a disorder. Confia’s current habit check-in does not measure hours, impaired control or functional impairment.

alcohol.title: Alcohol
alcohol.population: General population; risk depends on amount and context
alcohol.statistic: WHO states that no form of alcohol consumption is risk-free; risk depends on amount, frequency and personal factors.
alcohol.limitations: The current Confia entry does not reliably record beverage volume and alcohol concentration, so grams of ethanol cannot be calculated.

healthyDiet.title: Healthy diet
healthyDiet.population: General population; dietary needs vary by age, activity and health
healthyDiet.statistic: WHO guidance emphasizes a varied diet including whole grains, pulses, vegetables, fruit and appropriate protein sources. For adults, total fat should generally provide no more than 30% of energy, saturated fat less than 10%, trans fat less than 1%, and free sugars less than 10%.
healthyDiet.limitations: Confia records food categories and quantities but does not consistently capture product labels, whole-grain status, protein source, added sugars or fat composition. These entries cannot calculate an individual’s nutrient intake.
